# EnterpriseGlue v0.31.0 Release Notes

Generated from release-note fragments changed since `v0.30.1`.

## Highlights

- **oracle:** Add an optional required AES256 Oracle native network encryption profile across application pools, Oracle-capable images, deployment configuration, and qualification.
- **release-authorization:** Complete frozen release publication with source-bound image-workflow handoffs, authenticated package observations and retained security evidence without scanner caches.

## User and administrator impact

- Oracle application-database deployments can opt in to mandatory AES256 native network encryption independently of user SSO.
- Publication failures can resume the approved candidate without creating another software release or rebuilding its artifacts.
- Publication status distinguishes qualified, approved, publishing, partially published and verified published outcomes.
- Automatic chart/toolchain handoffs no longer mistake a decorated image-run title for a different workflow; package observations use the declared GitHub registry authentication.

## Upgrade and compatibility

- For existing Oracle databases, run the Oracle schema-owner migration before verify-only startup. Enabling native-aes256-required also requires the Oracle image and reviewed Oracle Net configuration.
- Install workflow plugin 0.1.16 and the reviewed protected-main publication workflows; use the frozen source and explicit recovery_prs when repairing an already qualified release.

## API and integration compatibility

- Add optional Oracle deployment configuration without changing default connection behavior.

## Configuration

- ORACLE_NETWORK_ENCRYPTION defaults to default; native-aes256-required enables mandatory AES256 NNE and requires ORACLE_NET_CONFIG_DIR.
- Explicit release dispatch retains source_ref, release_tag, release_pr and required_prs; optional recovery_prs lists every reviewed publication-only repair after the frozen source.
- Signed publication identities and append-only observations are stored in enterpriseglue-oss-release-publication on GHCR.
- Release Publication Reconcile automatically observes publisher completion. Manual resume=true renews approval and security acceptance before dispatching only incomplete publishers.
- GitHub history reads project merge state, branch names and labels one bounded page at a time; the workflow plugin advances independently to 0.1.16.
- Explicit prepare_replacement=true may supersede an unpublished reserved release PR and regenerate one replacement candidate at the same version. Neither tag nor GitHub release may exist.
- Publication artifacts retain named authority records, all ten architecture/role scan reports, vulnerability database metadata and observation evidence; the root-owned scanner cache is excluded.

## Database migrations

- Migration: ExpandOracleAssignmentKeys1700000000134 (Oracle only).
- Oracle assignment_key columns widen in place to VARCHAR2(4000 BYTE); values and indexes are preserved. Existing Oracle installations must apply this migration before verify-only application startup. Other database inventories and the PostgreSQL schema epoch remain unchanged.
- Application rollback retains the widened Oracle columns; automatic shrinking is refused.
- The publication-control changes introduce no database migration or application-runtime change. Other capabilities in this release retain their own migration requirements.
- Database rollback supported for the combined release: no.

## Security

- The required profile fails closed on invalid client configuration, unsupported transport overrides, missing Oracle Client libraries, and incompatible encryption negotiation.
- Oracle Net configuration is checked and read through the same open file with a bounded read. Optional image publication verifies protected-main authority and the API-resolved stable released source before checkout.
- Oracle image acceptance scans every committed application severity before browser qualification; publication retains the qualified bytes with signatures, CycloneDX SBOMs, and provenance.
- Automatic events remain non-publishing. Frozen batch ancestry, generated-document and managed-comment equality, exact candidate signatures and immutable payload hashes remain mandatory.
- Recovery requires explicit first-party repair PRs and a strict path allowlist. Application sources, dependency locks, package manifests, Dockerfiles, charts, migrations, scanner policy and unknown paths cannot qualify as publication-only repairs.
- Fresh scans cover all five exact image roles on AMD64 and ARM64 under the pinned scanner and unchanged severity/ignore policy, with current vulnerability database metadata and hashed reports.
- Unknown registry state and immutable conflicts stop recovery writes. Scratch canary records are marked as fixtures and cannot enter the production publication repository.
- Upstream publication authority binds the exact Docker Images workflow path, owning/head repositories, successful event and immutable source, while retaining protected-main, exact-tag and signed-candidate guards. Display titles are not workflow authority.

## Known limitations

- Client Oracle release-update and real identity-provider acceptance remain separate qualification gates.
- Observed registry publication does not establish Cloud installation, route promotion or production deployment.
- A content change requires a new generated document and qualified candidate; only reviewed publication-only repairs may reuse frozen artifacts.

## Rollback

- Application rollback retains the widened Oracle assignment-key columns; automatic schema shrinking is unsupported.
- Retain a previously qualified encrypted composition or stop service when deployment policy requires NNE; do not recover by disabling encryption.
- To roll back publication-control changes, revert the reviewed tooling and stop new recovery dispatches. Retain signed records and existing releases; never delete or repoint published tags. This tooling rollback requires no package or database rollback; follow the separate rollback guidance for other capabilities in the release.

## Validation evidence

- 60 focused Oracle contracts and 69 affected routing/native-SBOM/publication-authority/browser-preflight contracts passed; 183 CI contracts, 55 portability units, Helm positive/negative profiles and OpenShift rendering passed.

AES256 was observed before and after SSO, with four application sessions and zero unencrypted sessions after sign-in. Explicit rejection paths also passed on the local Bash runtime.
- The integrated local gate passed 181 CI contracts and the self-validating aggregate, 95 classifier/routing tests, 169 release-note/tooling tests, seven documentation-boundary tests, package-version discipline, both publisher policy checks, Actionlint and the combined diff check.
- The supplemental non-publishing authorization canary passed all 12 scenarios, including the actual verifier's rejection of an unstaged fixture candidate; it performed no publication or registry writes. Hosted protected CI, source-level non-publishing release readiness and the authorization canary also passed before PR #577 merged.
- The maintained immutable webhook schema requires the selected path and repository fields. The publication-control changes preserve application source, dependencies, database, package/chart payloads and scanner policy. Exact release-artifact and current security acceptance are required independently for the frozen release candidate.
